items.readable_text:
Content:
We can find or approximate volumes of real-world objects by representing them as right rectangular prisms.

Content:
For example, suppose that Timmy has [MATH: 12] wooden blocks. If each block measures [MATH: 3] centimeters long, [MATH: 4] centimeters wide, and [MATH: 2] centimeters high, what is the total volume of all the blocks combined?

Content:
First, we note that each block has the following dimensions:

Content:
- the length is [MATH: 3 \, \text{cm}]
- the width is [MATH: 4\, \text{cm}]
- the height is [MATH: 2 \, \text{cm}]

Content:
We can describe each block as a rectangular prism:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ec90cc0bc7c881839bfd9adaaff0c076]

Content:
So, the volume of each block is
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 3 × 4 × 2; = 24cm^{3}.]

Content:
Since Timmy has [MATH: 12] blocks, the total volume of all blocks combined is
[MATH: 12 \times 24 = 288 \, \text{cm}^3.]

- the width is [MATH: 4\, \text{cm}]
